ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated sanctions list, UK HMT sanctions, INTERPOL and domestic criminal-wanted lists, and Panama's national terrorism-financing list. PEP status is determined under Law 23 of 2015 as amended, covering domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs, family members, and close associates. Enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, source-of-wealth verification, enhanced ongoing monitoring, and annual CDD refreshes are mandatory for any PEP connection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Oficina Virtual de Reserva de Nombres (E-Registro; https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official language of registration. Corporate names may be constituted in Spanish, English, or any other language written in Latin-script characters. The standard corporation must include the statutory suffix 'S.A.' or the full form 'Sociedad Anónima'. Non-Spanish names are indexed in their original Latin-script form and, where used in Spanish-language instruments, the resident agent should annex a notarized Spanish translation to avoid registry objections.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Seguro / Insurance / Reaseguro / Reinsurance / Fianza / Surety
Valores / Securities / Bolsa / Exchange / Mercado de Valores
Fondo de Inversión / Investment Fund / Mutual Fund
Financiera / Finance / Crédito / Lending / Sistema de Pago / Payment System
Fundación / Foundation (reserved for entities constituted under Ley 25 de 1995)
Gobierno / Estado / República / Nacional / Oficial / Municipal / Panama
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon electronic rejection by the Registro Público: (1) the applicant or its resident agent may file a written recurso de reconsideración with the Dirección General del Registro Público within five (5) working days after electronic notification, attaching amended name options; (2) if reconsideration is denied, a recurso de apelación may be lodged with the Director General for hierarchical determination within the following five (5) working days; (3) in parallel, the applicant may re-apply online for a fresh name reservation, paying the statutory fee again and obtaining a new 30-day reservation window; (4) a final administrative denial may be challenged before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia through the contencioso-administrativo action within the statutory limitation period, with representation by an attorney admitted in Panama.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible at the registry level because the statutory registered office is the licensed resident agent's physical address in Panama. For the target designer-blind-box e-commerce business, a purely virtual arrangement does not satisfy the Dirección General de Ingresos (RUC), municipal Aviso de Operación, or banking and merchant-acquiring requirements if the company later claims a place of management in Panama; a serviced office, showroom, or operational logistics point is commercially recommended. Virtual-office acceptance is limited to registration and correspondence purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated below 5% per year for a standard commercial S.A. with no statutory license requirement; the probability rises to approximately 10-15% if the registered address is a high-density virtual mail facility or if the company applies for a local RUC, municipal license, or merchant account, as the tax authority and municipality may conduct unannounced verification visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Law No. 32 of 26 February 1927), as amended by Law No. 5 of 1997 and related statutes; provisions on incorporation, authorized capital, registered office, resident agent, directors and officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Dirección General de Registro, Sección de Sociedades Anónimas
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow-account requirement. The articles of incorporation fix an authorized capital, which may be issued in whole or in part without physical payment into an escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's preliminary report is approved and the subscription of the initial shares by the founding shareholders, as set out in the subscription agreement, is ratified. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation within the Republic of Panama is established at the address recorded with the registered agent, and the appointment of the registered agent is approved. RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary and Treasurer, to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the President and Secretary are authorized, jointly, to open banking accounts, sign contracts, and execute any supplementary instruments necessary to give effect to these resolutions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official portal: Sede Electrónica e-Tax (https://etax.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panamanian Sociedad Anónima must obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) through the DGI e-Tax portal after registration of the public deed (Escritura Pública) in the Registro Público de Panamá and appointment of a resident agent (agente residente). The RUC for a legal entity follows the format 3-XXX-XXXXXX-X. The initial application simultaneously triggers ITBMS registration and enrolment in the electronic invoicing system (SFEP). No minimum capital or physical local office is required; non-resident ownership is unrestricted. Foreign vendors with no local presence but with Panama domestic sales (including e-commerce via Shopify/Stripe) require RUC registration through the same portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation with Territorial_Scope: corporate income tax at 25% applies solely to Panama-source income; foreign-source income is not subject to Panamanian corporate tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists. Available elections: (i) simplified 'Régimen de Pequeño Contribuyente' for enterprises with annual gross income not exceeding PAB 300,000; (ii) Sede de Empresa Multinacional (SEM) licence under Law 41/2007 for qualified multinational export services, granting tax and immigration incentives; (iii) option to prepare the taxable basis under IFRS as accepted by DGI; (iv) election for definitive withholding on certain cross-border payments (retention regimes) under the Código Fiscal.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Value Added Tax transfer regime
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de-minimis threshold: every person habitually transferring taxable goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS upon obtaining a RUC. A lower simplified-regime threshold of PAB 300,000 in annual gross income applies for classification as 'Pequeño Contribuyente', subject to a fixed monthly quota instead of standard 7% filing.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory SFEP (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica de Panamá) under DGI Resolution 201-3804 of 2021. Taxpayers transmit invoices in real time via the e-Tax API; the DGI authorizes each invoice by returning a unique authorization code and embedded QR code. Large taxpayers have been mandatory since January 2022; all other registered taxpayers are phased into mandatory electronic issuance. Failure to obtain fiscal clearance nullifies the invoice for ITBMS input-credit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including designer blind-box toys) and qualifying offshore services are subject to ITBMS at 0% pursuant to Código Fiscal Articles 1082-H and 1082-I. The applicable conditions are: (a) sale concluded with a non-resident buyer; (b) physical departure of the goods from Panamanian territory evidenced by a DUDA export declaration; and (c) receipt of the export proceeds from abroad. ITBMS paid on inputs attributable to such export sales generates a creditable surplus (saldo a favor) refundable or offsettable against other tax liabilities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DUDA export customs declaration (Formulario Único de Aduanas) approved by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical exit from Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa del Exterior) issued by the Panamanian receiving bank
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract/purchase order
Export certificate and packaging list for customs verification where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audit teams cross-check the DUDA, bills of lading, and bank remittance certificates against the ITBMS return. If export proceeds are not repatriated and credited in Panama within 180 days, or if the export documentation is inconsistent, the transaction is re-characterized as a domestic taxable sale and assessed at 7% ITBMS, plus a 10% monthly surcharge under Article 716, default interest of 1.5% per month (or current legal DGI rate), and, in cases of fraud or fictitious exports, fines of up to 100% of the omitted tax under Article 760 and potential criminal prosecution for tax evasion under Law 1/2021 with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank exists in the Republic of Panama. The anchor currency is the US Dollar (USD) as legal tender under Decree-Law of 1904; the Balboa (PAB) exists solely as divisional coins pegged 1:1. Banking and FX oversight is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), while macroeconomic policy and SOE fiscal agency rest with the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF). There is no Foreign Exchange Administration; exchange operations are unregulated free-market activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and effective convertibility without capital controls. Current account and capital account transactions are equally freely convertible because the monetary base is USD itself; the PAB is nominal and counterside to the USD. Profit remittance and dividend distributions face no exchange-control barrier; a territorial-tax entity withholding outbound dividends to non-resident shareholders is generally exempt provided the beneficiary is not a Panamanian-sourced activity and formal documentation is filed. Anti-money-laundering (AML) Bank Secrecy Law obligations may delay large wire transfers until the underlying corporate beneficial-owner structure is disclosed to the bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender requirement. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no export-receipt deposit obligation. Export proceeds in USD may be retained offshore, used for import settlement, or repatriated at the exporter's discretion. Administrative reporting applies only to cash transactions above USD 10,000 and to the SBP/UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) threshold filings, not to FX conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Treasury Concentration Cash Management
Operational Account and Merchant Acquiring Settlement
Not viable for private S.A. treasury; public-sector fiscal agent only

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility, with structured constraints. Panama's legal framework (Law 15 of 2019 and SBP regulations on electronic payment systems) permits licensed 'Sociedades de Emisión y Medios de Pago Electrónicos' (EMIs) to issue e-money and payment instruments in USD. For the designer-toy merchant, platforms such as Wise, Payoneer, dLocal, and Banking-as-a-Service rails via local banking partners can serve as collection and disbursement adjuncts; however, they should not replace a Tier-1 commercial bank. Key constraints: (i) settlement to a Panamanian corporate account requires a local partner bank; (ii) UAF and SBP transaction monitoring applies to e-money flows and cross-border settlement (over USD 10,000 triggers enhanced reports); (iii) onboarding of a holding S.A. holding electronically signed board resolutions is accepted by leading EMIs but generally requires a passport, apostilled incorporation certificate, and a UBO declaration. A full treasury reliance on an offshore EMI without a local bank account is legally imprudent and operationally fragile.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is legally permissible under SBP prudential standards when a robust risk-based non-face-to-face client due diligence process is implemented (video identity verification, digital board authorization, certified document authentication). In practice, Tier-1 Panamanian banks require either (i) physical presence of at least one director or (ii) an in-country authorized legal representative holding a public power-of-attorney granted before a Panamanian Notary, plus a source-of-wealth interview for any corporate entity with foreign shareholders. Full remote opening with apostilled documents is available but typically downgrades onboarding to Medium risk, triggering higher approval levels and extended turn-around time. It is recommended that the President of the S.A. and the Compliance Officer of the beneficial owner physically visit Panama City for the account-opening session and obtain a bank reference to avoid rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated Panamanian S.A. with nominee shareholders or bearer-share structure history; UBO registry not yet updated
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled Registered Articles of Incorporation from the Registro Público de Panamá; UBO declaration (Declaración de Beneficiario Final) filed and receipted; certificate of good standing; notarized resignation letters of any nominee officers; a legal opinion from a licensed Panamanian attorney confirming economic substance and beneficial ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between low physical footprint of a vinyl toy manufacturer (rotocasting/airbrush finishing) and expected e-commerce sales velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for the production/hand-finishing facility in Panama; utility and telecom bills in the entity's name; payroll records and CSS (Caja de Seguro Social) contribution receipts; purchase orders for PVC resin and packaging materials; inventory photographs or storage warehouse contracts; audited or internally prepared inventory count sheets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiary or counterparty country exposure in outbound trade disbursements (e.g., China, Mexico) triggering enhanced due diligence on trade settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid underlying commercial contracts, proforma invoices, bill of lading/AWB, packaging list, commercial invoice, and customs exit declarations (Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas); copies of prior export transactions proving consistent trade pattern; statement of transaction purpose with HS/ISIC codes aligned to 3240 manufacturer scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or non-typical retail e-commerce proceeds from Shopify/Stripe without platform settlement statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly Shopify Payments / Stripe settlement reports; net-revenue screenshots and payout history; list of marketplace SKUs; customer refund policy and clear tax invoices for retail goods; reconciliation with bank deposits; explanation of chargeback/sales-tax reserve amounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Approved protocol comprises an SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer from the shareholder's overseas bank to the Panamanian S.A.'s operational account at a Tier-1 bank. Because Panama has no exchange controls, there is no mandated currency purpose code; nevertheless, standard bank remittance instructions require field 70 (Remittance Information) to state 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION — SHAREHOLDER CONTRIBUTION

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For local Panama suppliers and employee payroll in USD/PAB, use the ACH Panama electronic clearing system via the local account (same-day USD settlement). For international material and finished-product disbursements (Asian factories, packaging suppliers), settlement rail is SWIFT MT103 (free-form wire, no FX conversion since USD is account base) or an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) opened through the Panamanian bank for larger batch orders. At least one LC confirmation from a prime bank in the supplier's jurisdiction ensures bank-to-bank indemnity and documented trade-chain clearing. For e-commerce refunds and market-creating in local markets in the Americas, use the principal bank's global payment network or, for lower amounts, a licensed EMI card/POS rail from local payment processors. All outbound trade disbursements must be aligned with the underlying clearance invoice; Panama does not impose Form-1042 withholding on imports, but customs-Aduanero controls apply to plastic resin imports and export of finished designer toys.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts on EUR/CNY/GBP receivables executed with the Panamanian bank's offshore treasury desk (no onshore Balboa forward market because PAB/USD is pegged at 1:1).
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in Chinese Renminbi (CNY) for PVC-resin import hedging, using the regional trade corridor through a correspondent bank in Hong Kong or Singapore.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and USD/CNY) permitted for confirmed purchase orders in the toy retail value chain, with SBP reporting in the banks' regulatory returns; must be limited to hedges of firm trade exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas) – electronic payment via DGI SIR portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 15 of each calendar year, irrespective of revenue or activity level
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus 1% monthly interest; denial of Paz y Salvo (tax clearance); sustained default triggers suspension of corporate rights and administrative strike-off by the Registro Público

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta, Form 110) – required even for dormant or zero-revenue companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) via SIR e-filing platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 15 following a calendar fiscal year-end; within 3 months after any non-calendar fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment recargo (10%) plus 1% monthly interest; statutory fines up to USD 1,000 for failure to file; DGI presumed-assessment power; persistent non-compliance supports administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Re-Confirmation (Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 calendar days after each incorporation anniversary; UBO changes arising from share transfers must also be reported within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of USD 300 to USD 1,000 per infraction; blocking of tax-clearance certificates and of registrable corporate acts; risk of administrative strike-off and director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business Patent Renewal (Patente Municipal / Aviso de Operación) – applicable only when the entity operates physically within Panamanian territory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipio de Panamá or the competent district municipality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before January 31 for the operative calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal recargo of 10% plus monthly interest; fines up to USD 500; suspension or closure of the business license for continued non-renewal

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Panamanian-licensed CPA when annual gross revenue reaches USD 1,000,000 or total assets reach USD 2,000,000, or when the DGI designates the entity as a large taxpayer; financial institutions, insurers, and securities-market participants are always audited under sectoral regulation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama; small and medium entities may apply IFRS for SMEs, while large and public-interest entities apply full IFRS; statutory books must be maintained in Spanish with figures in USD

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual re-confirmation filed on the DGI UBO Registry within 15 days after the incorporation anniversary; every share transfer must be endorsed in the share register and, where the bylaws require, approved by the board of directors, with the resulting UBO change declared within 15 days; the bearer-share framework was eliminated, and all shareholdings are registered and fully traceable
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members with continuous share transfer history
Register of Directors and Officers with election and removal records
Minute Book of shareholders' and board resolutions
Share transfer ledger and share certificate stubs
Resident agent's statutory corporate file (bylaws, amendments, UBO records)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 8,000 for a small merchandising entity; not triggered below the USD 1,000,000 audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (general corporate rate, Art. 699 Código Fiscal as amended by Law 8 of 2010); graduated micro scale: 15% on the first B/.50,000 of net taxable income for fiscally small companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial sourcing (Art. 694): profits economically earned outside Panama (cross-border DTC sales exported from Panama and managed abroad) fall outside ISR; legally available preferential regimens: Multinational Headquarters (SEM) Law 41/2007, Colon Free Zone, Panama Pacifico — none qualified for a rotocasting/injection toy manufacturing shop without credible local production substance; limited deduction acceleration (2% annual depreciation for industrial equipment per Código Fiscal Tarifa B).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 401 Declaración de Renta (Personas Jurídicas) - annual income tax return; mandatory e-filing via DGI T@x 365 (dgi.gob.pa) or certified DAT software; supplementary Form 425 for transfer pricing when thresholds are met and Form 401-D for dividend WHT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Form 401); advance ISR installments/estimated payments are remitted on 1.5% of gross revenue (or 100% of previous year's tax) with two semiannual payments where applicable; withholding returns Form 402/403 monthly; dividend WHT per distribution with monthly/quarterly deposit.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year; a calendar-year company must file no later than 31 March of the following year; up to two 3-month extensions may be sought with prior DGI approval but tax must be provisionally paid when extensions are granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from Panama-source sales of designer blind-box toys (rotocasting, airbrushing, injection-molded vinyl art figures) and ancillary freight/recovery charges invoiced to buyers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only sales physically performed, delivered or exploited in Panama. E-commerce transfers where title, risk and delivery pass abroad (FOB Panama port or ex-works) are foreign-source and excluded. If zero, leave blank on face but attach foreign-sales schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Export revenues governed by Territorial Rule: foreign-source income, dividends received, SEM-approved international services, fixed-term bank deposit interest attributable to foreign markets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident S.A. with no Panama activities must document exemption via bills of lading, shipping e-logistics (Shopify/Stripe) transaction ledgers and customer country taxonomy; disputed safe-harbor submissions attract full 25% assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct production costs: PVC resin, plastic pellets, spray paints, molding machinery depreciation, irreversible casting tools, packaging SKUs and direct labor actually hired in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only if supported by Panamanian statutory books (Libro de Inventarios and Libro Mayor accessory cost schedules); non-residents holding source records outside Panama risk automatic 3% gross-base minimum tax adjustment (Art. 699-A).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: studio/showroom rent, marketing (Meta Ads, TikTok, Shopify), royalties paid for licensed art IP, customs, air-freight, professional fees, registered agent and miscellaneous administrative spends capped at Art. 702 relatability rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenditures connected to Panama-source sales; contested cross-border marketing and platform fees must be allocated on OECD TP principles (benefit test) if paid to related parties elsewhere; intellectual-property license payments to a related non-resident require Form 425 schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income computed as Box 101 less Boxes 102-104, before loss offsets; NOL absorption allowed for carry-forward years under Art. 699-B (up to five years from the loss year).
Income tax computed at the 25% statutory rate on Box 105, subject to progressive micro-scale (15% bracket) where eligible, and reduced by the 3% over-gross minimum tax alternative when applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fill if any Panama-source income exists; a non-resident never files a nil return merely because the S.A. was incorporated — the S.A. itself is the taxpayer and must file regardless of the shareholder's residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable prepayments: collected withholding certificates, monthly/quarterly anticipo installments, CIF (currency/credit) withholding and any foreign tax credit allowed under a signed Panama DTA application on Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach DGI-issued withholding certificates (Form 402) and TRC annexure; treaty credits claimed by the non-resident parent do not reduce the Panamanian S.A.'s liability and cannot be entered here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 108 - Saldo a pagar / saldo a favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Difference between Boxes 106 and 107; refunds are payable in 12 months from the lodgement date, with statutory monthly interest accrual on late refunds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due must be paid through the Panamanian banking system (B/. or USD); DGI does not accept foreign payment gateways; persistent nil-balance declarations from a cash-generative online seller are a red-flag trigger for an ex officio 10% presumptive assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of a month up to 100% of the tax (Art. 715); non-computable returns: B/.50-B/.5,000 daily-validated minimum fines; overdue balances accrue 1.5% monthly interest (Article 744); failure to file six months post-deadline allows DGI business closure (cierre de local) and the compulsory registry of the taxpayer as 'in mora' blocking export permits and re-entry of directors from Panama borders; e-Tax portal technical validation failures do not suspend these deadlines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% final withholding on dividends and profit distributions paid out of profits that have been taxed at the corporate level (Art. 733-734 Código Fiscal); 10% where distributions derive from exempt or foreign-source funds; additional advance-dividend WHT is prepaid at the corporate level (5% for taxed profits / 10% exempt profits) and imputed as a credit against the 5%-10% definitive tax on the shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network is deliberately narrow and position-sensitive (in force: Barbados, Mexico, Republic of Korea, Taiwan/Chinese Taipei, UAE, Qatar; signed-not-in-force: Spain, Italy, Switzerland). Administrative protocol for reduced rates: (1) beneficial owner obtains a DGI Certificado de Residencia Fiscal (TRC) through the registered agent, evidencing effective management, business premises, and Book/Article 694 substance; (2) the Panamanian withholding agent (the S.A.) submits the TRC plus OECD-compliant residence declaration and, where the DTA so requires, an official AEOI/FATCA registration number; (3) reduced WHT is applied ex parte by the payer and substantiated in the Form 401-D dividend annexure; the DGI Large Taxpayers' Office may challenge the application within 5 years if the shareholder lacks economic substance or treaty-shopping motive is shown.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties/technical assistance for IP exploitation within Panama are Panama-source and attract 25% statutory final WHT collection from the gross payment (arts. 694, enforcement practice; non-treaty). Interest paid by a Panama S.A. to a non-resident lender is outside the Panamanian tax net when the lender carries no Panama establishment and the loan is contracted abroad (0% WHT); under ratified DTAs, interest treaty rates commonly 5%-10% and royalties 10%-15% (e.g., Panama-Mexico treaty: 10% royalties and reduced interest if not attributable to Panama PE; any treaty benefit requires simultaneous Form 425 documentation of the underlying cross-border payments).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.2,000,000 (USD 2 million, fixed Balboa parity) in aggregate related-party cross-border transactions during a fiscal year triggers mandatory (a) Form 425 annual transfer pricing return (due 30 June following the fiscal close) and (b) preparation and surrender on demand of the Local File (Informe Local de Precios de Transferencia) and Master File (Informe Maestro); transactions between the S.A. and its foreign licensor parent for the 'DEADLY BLIND BOX' artwork IP, procurement of vinyl resin and bulk freight are the relevant lines.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Comparable Uncontrolled Price (CUP) - preferred for raw vinyl resin procurement and mass-produced B2B toy components
Resale Price Method - applicable to the local distributor/showroom resale of finished designed-blind-box series
Cost Plus Method - applicable to contract machining, rotocasting and airbrushing services rendered to group companies
Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) - recommended benchmark for the economic-return test of the Panamanian production entity
Profit Split Method - used where two affiliates jointly own the designer-toy IP and apportion residual profit from global royalties
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not impose a UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulation; the doctrine enters Panamanian law through (1) Art. 694 territorial sourcing (profits must arise from actual panameño-based operations), (2) the SEM/HQ regime (Law 41/2007, Decree 3/2016) requiring genuine office, local payroll and senior management decisions in-country, (3) Law 47 of 2013 prohibiting anonymous bearer shares - all bearer shares must be immobilized and beneficial ownership filed in the Shareholders' Register at the Public Registry, and (4) the OECD Inclusive Framework commitment that forces DGI to deny treaty/regime advantages to a shell. A rotocasting/injection workshop S.A. that can show physical meters, utility bills, form 401 payroll declarations and Customs export records satisfies the doctrine; an S.A. acting purely as a Shopify invoicing pass-through with no inventory or staff is recharacterized as wholly artificial and loses the territorial exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: False reporting or suppression of e-commerce collection, under-declaring Shopify/Stripe balances on Box 101, fabricating raw-material invoices to inflate Box 103 COGS, destroying order ledgers, or classifying Panamanian licensing royalties as non-taxable foreign-source profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal defraudación fiscal (Código Fiscal Arts. 712-C to 712-E as amended by Law 76 of 2019): prison term of 2 to 5 years and pecuniary fine of twice to ten times the tax evaded, plus reinstated tax and non-waivable interest at 1.5% monthly; DGI also files the 'Lista de Contribuyentes en Mora' blocking import/export screening and VAT (ITBMS) licences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or legal representatives who sign or consent to the false Form 401 are deemed handlers of the evasion (Código Fiscal Art. 712-G): joint and several civil liability for the corporate debt; levying preventive embargo of personal accounts, a 180-day travel ban pending indictment, and extradition if the director is a foreign national. The Public Registry may cancel the S.A.'s licence upon DGI certification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Abuse / Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the S.A. solely as a pass-through billing vehicle (invoicing the designer-toy brand, paying third-party factories abroad) while enjoying territorial exemptions; refusing to register the beneficial owner in the Registro de Accionistas; transferring bearer shares without immobilization; claiming non-resident status in a beneficiary jurisdiction without any local operation of the S.A.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: For Law 47 of 2013 bearer-share breaches: fine from B/.5,000 to B/.50,000 and the shares become unenforceable; commercial operations may be suspended by the Superintendencia de Empresas (SEP?); tax consequences: elimination of territorial exclusion, reclassification of all global sales as Panamanian (25% ISR) and automatic 10% dividend WHT on distributions from reclassified funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil piercing under the fraud-in-the-law doctrine (Reforma de la Ley 5 de 2009?): directors jointly liable for the full tax difference; the DGI can embargo personal assets without court order when the S.A. is reduced to an alter ego; directors are flagged in the UAF database, and during criminal proceedings the Travel Judge (Juzgado de Garantías) may order an arrest warrant for the beneficial owner (non-punishable shell scheme) if linked to AML predicate proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / FINANCING OF INTELLECTUAL-PROPERTY TRADING (AML Case)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly accepting large (B/.10,000+) anonymous payments for limited-edition blind-box figures, executing wire splits to bypass the B/.10,000 threshold, mixing company proceeds with personal accounts, failing to run customer/beneficial-owner due diligence, or misrepresenting the S.A.'s ownership to open a Stripe/Shopify Payments merchant account (KYC fraud).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law 23 of 2015 (as reformed by Law 70 of 2019) criminalizes money laundering with 5 to 12 years' imprisonment (sg. 15 years for organized crime facilitators), extinción de dominio (forfeiture) of all traced proceeds, corporate/institutional fines up to B/.5 million, and cancellation of the company's licence to operate; the S.A. also loses the territorial exception because laundered funds are constructively Panama-source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the 2019 reforms, a director who manages, finances or conceals the operation of a laundering scheme is a 'autore de lavado' — no corporate veil available: preventive detention, restraining orders over passports, freezing of linked commercial accounts, and disqualification from holding positions in any regulated Panamanian entity for 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Dividend Distribution Defaults
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to the non-resident sole shareholder without declaring/paying the 5% (or 10%) dividend WHT; filing Form 401-D with artificial 'reexport' excuses; recharacterizing trademark-royalty payments as 'consulting' to avoid 25% royalties WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The unpaid WHT becomes an immediate personal statutory debt of the S.A. (Art. 733); surcharge of 100% of the deficiency (Art. 744? — actually 'recargo del 100%' applies to withheld amounts never declared) plus 1.5% monthly interest, publication in the 'morosidad' register, and possible reconduction of the shareholders to the 35% patrimonial tax regime on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate officers are personally liable when they were the withholding agents in fact: joint and several liability for the withheld amounts, penalty, interest and procedural costs; failure to comply triggers a personal 'visa bar' via the DGI-Migración interlock, meaning the responsible director cannot travel on Panamanian passports or renew work permits until full settlement is secured.
